To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the H i disks of 6 massive edge-on spirals are tilted with respect to the stellar disks, that the H i disk of NGC 973 is warped, that the H I disk of NGC 5908 is warped along the line of site, that the H1 disk of IC 253 is warped, that NGC 5529 shows signs of a radial gas flow, that the H 1 disk of NGC 4207 is warped, that a dwarf companion is detected at 36 k
the gas disks in the galaxies we studied have a variety of morphologies, including warps and flares, and that the inner disks of three galaxies show signs of ongoing interaction.
the gas disks in the sample are generally warped and that the outer regions in three of the galaxies are likely the result of recent interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the formation and evolution of galaxies and their central supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the context of the cosmic web; (ii) the role of the interstellar medium and star formation in the growth of galaxies; (iii) the physics of starburst galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGNs); and (iv) the evolution of galaxies in the local Universe.
the study of the interplay between gas, dust, dark matter and stars in a sample of massive edge-on galaxies.
the study of the interstellar medium of galaxies, in particular the atomic gas, and the role it plays in the formation and evolution of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atomic hydrogen gas disks in edge-on spirals are not as simple and regular as often thought.

the atomic gas disks of the 6 galaxies studied in this paper show a variety of interesting features and signs of interaction with their surroundings, which are not necessarily connected to the ongoing interaction between NGC 973 and its companion.
the H i gas in the disk of the Milky Way is not in a stable configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the gas distribution is complex in all but one of the galaxies.
our modelling has provided new insight into the structure and dynamics of the atomic gas in these galaxies and revealed signs of recent interactions in some of them.
the gas disks in our sample of edge-on spirals are warped and/or flaring, but not in a way that can be explained by simple models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H i disks in our sample are highly structured and complex, which makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions on the origin and evolution of the gas in these galaxies.
the atomic gas disks of massive edge-on spiral are not always regular.

the H i disks of massive edge-on galaxies are complex and show a variety of features that are related to the interaction with other galaxies, to the presence of spiral structure, or to the interaction of the disk with its dark matter halo.
